headline: AGNICO EAGLE BETS C$57M ON ABITIBI JUNIOR — 10.45% STAKE IN RADISSON MINING BACKS FIRST UNDERGROUND PROGRAM AT O'BRIEN GOLD
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines (NYSE: AEM) entered a C$57.2M strategic investment in Radisson Mining Resources (TSX-V: RMRDF) on August 24, acquiring 53,420,000 units at C$1.07 — a 6% premium to last close and 19% above the 20-day VWAP. Each unit includes one share plus a half-warrant exercisable at C$1.39 for 60 months, giving Agnico ~10.45% undiluted (14.90% partly diluted). The funds launch an advanced underground exploration program at Radisson's O'Brien Gold Project in the Bousquet-Cadillac corridor, where historic production grades exceeded 15 g/t. In the Abitibi at $4,673 gold, a major producer paying a 19% VWAP premium for a 10% stake is one of the clearest high-conviction signals retail investors can observe: it represents professional validation before the broader market reprices the asset.

headline: GREENLAND MINES' SARFARTOQ HOLDS 40,700 TONNES OF NdPr OXIDE — FIVE YEARS OF EX-CHINA MAGNET SUPPLY IN FIRST-EVER INDICATED RESOURCE
snippet: Greenland Mines Ltd. (NASDAQ: GRML) delivered the first-ever public Indicated Mineral Resource for its Sarfartoq Nd-Pr magnet rare earths project in southwest Greenland: a hybrid open pit/underground scenario showing 6.9 million tonnes at 1.60% TREO (Indicated) plus 5.3 million tonnes at 0.96% TREO (Inferred), totalling 12.2 million tonnes at 1.32% TREO. The combined resource contains approximately 40,700 tonnes of NdPr oxide — equivalent to roughly five years of all NdPr oxide refined outside China in 2025 — enriched in the four critical magnet rare earths: neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium. The resource is the first public technical report in the project's 15-year history to include an Indicated category, arriving as China's rare earth export restrictions have pushed allied nations to accelerate every non-Chinese NdPr development in their pipeline.

headline: TERRONERA MINE BACK ONLINE — ENDEAVOUR SILVER ENDS 12-DAY EJIDO BLOCKADE IN JALISCO, PRODUCTION RESUMES AUGUST 24
snippet: Endeavour Silver Corp. (TSX: EDR / NYSE: EXK) announced on August 23 that the illegal blockade at its Terronera Mine in Jalisco, Mexico has been removed and full operations will resume August 24. The mine — one of the few new primary silver operations opened globally in the past two years — was suspended August 12 when members of the nearby Ejido community established a peaceful blockade over concerns about road maintenance, water supply control, medical services, and financial assistance. Terronera was just seven months into commercial production when the stoppage began. With silver trading near $68-69 per ounce, the 12-day suspension removed a meaningful portion of monthly primary silver output from one of Mexico's highest-grade new mines; the resumption restores margin-positive production at a time when primary silver supply growth globally is severely constrained.

headline: COMSTOCK LODE CHANGES HANDS — MACKAY PRECIOUS METALS CLOSES $45M+ NEVADA SILVER DISTRICT DEAL, DRILLING COMMENCES
snippet: Comstock Inc. received $20 million in cash and closed the sale of its mineral, mining, processing and real estate assets in Nevada's historic Comstock Lode district to Mackay Precious Metals Inc. — an aggregate transaction valued at more than $45 million. Separately, Mackay Gold & Silver mobilized a diamond core drill rig to the 100%-owned Comstock District project in Nevada and commenced drilling as of August 20, 2026. The Comstock Lode produced over 400 million ounces of silver-equivalent between 1859 and 1882 and is undergoing a modern exploration revival as silver prices approach $70 per ounce. A $45M transaction creating an actively drilling junior on one of North America's most storied silver districts at current metal prices is a structural positive for the sector.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: SILVER DOWN 47% FROM $121 JANUARY RECORD WITH A 6TH YEAR OF DEFICITS — THE CASE FOR BUYING WHEN NOBODY'S WATCHING
snippet: GoldSilver.com's August 2026 silver analysis documents a striking divergence: silver has fallen approximately 35-47% from its January 2026 record of $121.62 per ounce, yet the structural supply deficit is entering its sixth consecutive year with a projected shortfall of 46.3 million ounces in 2026. Mine production rose just 3% in 2025 to 846.6 million ounces and is expected to stay flat because roughly 75% of silver arrives as a byproduct of copper, lead, and zinc mining where output follows those metals' economics. China officially reclassified silver from an ordinary commodity to a strategic material on January 1, 2026; Russia, India, and Saudi Arabia have joined the central bank accumulation trend. The GoldSilver framework: price fell while the deficit did not — the textbook setup of maximum retail disinterest before the physical reality reasserts at higher prices.

headline: GOLD MINERS' Q2 UNIT PROFIT HIT $2,787/oz — GDXJ'S TOP 25 AISC JUST 28.8% OF SPOT; GDX P/E SITS AT 16.5x
snippet: A post-Q2 2026 fundamentals analysis finds gold averaged $4,512 in the quarter (up 37.3% YoY) while all-in sustaining costs fell 5.1% to $1,298 per ounce, generating $2,787/oz implied unit profits — the second-highest on record after Q1 2026's $3,129. The GDX top-25 generated collective Q2 revenue of $35.98 billion, operating cash flow of $17.22 billion, and $12.30 billion in bottom-line profits. Despite these extraordinary fundamentals, GDX-25 trailing P/E stands at just 16.5x while GDXJ-25's AISCs as a percentage of gold hit a record-low 28.8% in Q2. Newmont posted $2.2B in record Q2 free cash flow; Agnico Eagle achieved a record $1.33B. The analysis argues institutional models priced for $2,500-$3,000 gold cannot survive a third consecutive quarter of $2,700+ unit profits — a repricing trigger arriving with Q3 earnings in October.

headline: COPPER ABOVE $14,000 AFTER LME EXPIRY — WHY 42 CONSECUTIVE INVENTORY DECLINES MEAN THE SQUEEZE ISN'T DONE
snippet: Following the August 19 LME prompt-date expiry, Crux Investor argues the structural conditions sustaining copper above $14,000 per tonne remain fully intact. LME warehouse stocks stand at 204,975 tonnes — down 42 consecutive sessions from 389,425 on May 29, the longest uninterrupted inventory decline since 2014 — with nearly half of remaining stocks already cancelled for withdrawal. The cash-to-3-month spread continues to hold near $434 per tonne, far above historical norms, because the underlying supply constraints have not changed: the Kamoa-Kakula seismic flood (57,000t Zijin shortfall for 2026), lower Chilean production from Codelco, and the Freeport Gresik smelter outage in Indonesia all continue to constrain new material entering the LME system. The August 19 expiry removed speculative short-covering pressure; it did not restore supply. For TSX-V and ASX copper explorers, the post-expiry hold above $14,000 strengthens the structural case for greenfield copper discoveries in tier-one jurisdictions.

headline: STERLING METALS ABSORBS QCX GOLD TODAY — 99.79% SHAREHOLDER VOTE SEALS ABITIBI GOLD CONSOLIDATION ON EXPECTED AUG 25 CLOSE
snippet: Sterling Metals Corp. (TSX-V: SAG) is expected to complete its all-share arrangement with QcX Gold Corp. (TSX-V: QCX) on or around August 25, 2026, after QcX shareholders approved the deal with 99.79% of votes cast in favour at an August 18 meeting. Sterling is acquiring QcX's Abitibi gold assets by issuing 0.20789 Sterling shares per QcX share. Both companies explore in the Abitibi Greenstone Belt — the world's most productive gold district — and the consolidation creates a larger combined land package at a time when Agnico Eagle simultaneously made a C$57M strategic investment in a neighbouring O'Brien Gold asset. The Abitibi is seeing record drill activity as $4,673 gold makes historically marginal systems economic: the two deals announced within hours of each other on August 24-25 signal that mid-size and major producers are actively positioning in the district.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: PCE WEDNESDAY, WARSH FRIDAY, GDP REVISION IN BETWEEN — THREE DATA PRINTS THAT COULD SET GOLD'S SEPTEMBER DIRECTION
snippet: GoldSilver.com's August 25 gold price outlook maps the three sequential macro data prints arriving this week that will collectively determine September gold positioning: Wednesday's July Core PCE deflator (forecast +0.3%), the Q2 GDP revision (tracking near stall speed), and Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole address Friday at ~10 a.m. ET. Recent jobs, CPI, and PPI prints all came in soft, reducing September rate-hike odds from 50% to 31% — a structural shift that favours bullion. Central banks purchased a quarterly record 288.9 tonnes in Q2 2026 even as prices fell. The analysis identifies $4,500 as the structural floor where central bank and physical demand re-enter, and argues neither an inflationary PCE nor a weak GDP print is unambiguously negative for gold given the U.S. fiscal dominance backdrop — leaving the Warsh speech as the only print that carries genuine tail-risk for bullion this week.

headline: TREASURY DOUBLES BOND BUYBACK TO $4B/SESSION — GOLD HOLDS ABOVE $4,645 TUESDAY AS MARKET PRICE IN STRUCTURAL YIELD SUPPRESSION
snippet: Gold held above $4,645 Tuesday August 25 after the U.S. Treasury unexpectedly doubled its long-term bond buyback program to $4 billion per session — up from the $2 billion scale initially attributed to Treasury Secretary Bessent's 'Treasury Twist' operation. The doubling compresses long-duration yields and structurally weakens the dollar without requiring Federal Reserve action, providing a gold-positive tailwind that is independent of this week's Jackson Hole event risk. Silver September futures climbed to $69.53, up approximately 14% month-over-month in August's best precious metals performance since 2020. For retail investors positioning ahead of the week's PCE-GDP-Warsh triple event, the Treasury buyback expansion is arguably more durable than any single Fed speech outcome: it is an administratively controlled mechanism that can be expanded further without congressional or FOMC approval.
